title: A universally closed morphism of schemes is quasi-compact
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a universally closed morphism of schemes is quasi-compact, so that universal closedness cannot hold for a morphism that fails to be quasi-compact (statement lines 9985-9991). The counted proof is a contrapositive argument of real substance: after reducing to an affine base it builds an auxiliary affine space with one coordinate per affine chart of the source, cuts out a closed subset of the fibre product encoding the failure of the charts to cover, produces a point over a strategically chosen bad point of the base that escapes the image on that fibre, and then uses a polynomial vanishing on the image together with the invertibility of one coefficient to construct a point of the closed subset whose image avoids the zero locus of that polynomial, contradicting closedness (proof lines 9993-10047). It is H2: every step is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are standard criteria for quasi-compactness and for points of fibre products.
